title: Recycling and caring for Earth
examples: What should I do with this empty juice box?
Is throwing things away always bad for the Earth?
How can we use less electricity at home?

explain.say: Today we learn how to care for our Earth. We learn three big ways to help. These ways are reduce, reuse, and recycle.
Reduce means using less stuff. We can use less water when we brush teeth. We can also use fewer paper towels each day. This keeps things from becoming trash.
Reuse means using things again for a new job. An old jar can hold crayons for art time. A plastic bottle can become a toy boat. We give things a second life.
Recycle means sending old things to a special place. Paper, plastic, and metal can be recycled. These materials make brand new things later on.
We must never litter on the ground. Litter means dropping trash where it does not belong. Always use a bin for your wrappers and bottles.

faq.q: What is the difference between littering and recycling?
faq.a: Littering is dropping trash anywhere, which hurts animals and the ground. Recycling is putting clean materials in the right bin to be made into new things.
asks: What should I do with my wrappers?

faq.q: Can I recycle anything that is dirty?
faq.a: It is best to rinse things out a little bit first. Clean items recycle much better than dirty ones.
asks: Must things be clean to recycle?

faq.q: Does saving energy only mean turning off lights?
faq.a: No, saving energy also means walking instead of taking a car sometimes. It also means not leaving electronics plugged in when not used.
asks: How else can I save energy?

faq.q: What does 'reduce' really mean for me?
faq.a: It means thinking before you buy something new. Can you really use this item, or will it just become trash?

faq.q: If I reuse a plastic bottle, does it count as recycling?
faq.a: No, reusing is using it again yourself. Recycling is sending it to a factory to be remade into something else.
asks: Is reusing the same as recycling?
What is the difference between the two?

facts: Recycling saves energy needed to make new items.
Littering can harm wildlife habitats greatly.
Using less water helps save Earth's resources.
Reusing items keeps them out of landfills.

quiz.say: You have an old t-shirt. You decide to cut it up and use it as cleaning rags. Which action did you take?
quiz.why: You used the item again for a different purpose instead of throwing it away.

wrong.0: Littering means throwing it on the ground.
wrong.2: Recycling means sending it to a special factory bin.
wrong.3: Reducing means using less of something from the start.

quiz.say: You see a plastic water bottle on the playground ground. What should you do?

options.show: Put it in the recycling bin
options.say: Put it in the recycling bin

quiz.why: It is a recyclable material, so the bin is the correct place.

wrong.0: Leaving it there is littering and hurts the Earth.
wrong.1: While you could reuse it, the bin is the best place for it.
wrong.2: Burning trash makes bad smoke for the air.

quiz.say: To help save energy at school, which action is best?
quiz.why: Turning off lights when leaving rooms stops electricity from being wasted.

wrong.0: Leaving the door open lets energy escape outside.
wrong.1: Playing loud music does not save any energy.
wrong.2: Keeping them on uses up electricity even when not needed.
